title: Rework slot allocator and add scheduler telemetry to reduce tail latency
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary:
We frequently observe tail latency spikes when a mix of short and long requests contend for batcher lanes and KV cache warmup. The current continuous batching controller ties slot allocation and eviction heuristics into a single hot path, which is hard to reason about and blocks other recent optimizations. This ticket will: 1) separate the slot allocator from the batching commit path, 2) introduce epoch-based KV cache checkpointing to reduce synchronous eviction work, and 3) add scheduler-level telemetry and traces to make root-cause analysis tractable.

Goals:
- Reduce 95th/99th percentile token-latency by 15-25% under mixed workloads.
- Make slot allocation logic modular and testable (unit/integration).
- Add telemetry so we can answer: which allocations caused stalls, eviction vs kernel scheduling delays, and tenant fairness violations.

Scope and approach:
- New slot allocator component (non-blocking API) that hands out soft-reservations to batchers. Batchers commit using a lightweight lease token; the allocator maintains fairness counters per-tenant and per-priority lane.
- Decouple eviction: switch to epoch-based checkpointing for KV cache where evictions are amortized by background GC worker. The fast path will only check for lease validity, not perform synchronous compaction.
- Scheduler telemetry: add structured traces for allocation decision, lease grant, eviction trigger, and commit latency. Emit metrics: allocator_grants, allocator_denials, lease_stalls, kv_epoch_gc_duration, per-lane_backpressure, per-tenant_starvation_time.
- Dependency updates required: bump tokio to 1.28 (for cooperative task yielding improvements), update parking_lot to 0.13, and upgrade metrics crate to support histogram buckets used by observability team. Verify no breaking changes via CI.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for slot allocator covering fairness and lease expiration semantics.
- Integration test that reproduces previous tail-latency regression locally and shows improvement in CI load job.
- Telemetry dashboards created (links below) showing allocator and KV epoch metrics.
- Canary rollout plan executed with no customer-facing errors on two Dedicated clusters and two private customers.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch with allocator behind runtime flag. Run canary load with internal traffic.
2) Gradually enable on 5% of hosted requests for 48 hours while monitoring allocator_denials and lease_stalls.
3) If metrics stable, promote to 25% then 100% over a week.
4) If regressions detected, auto-fallback to legacy allocator by runtime flag and trigger rollback playbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: background GC could overconsume GPU memory bandwidth during peak. Mitigation: rate-limit GC worker and cap concurrency per-device; add GC backoff on kernel contention signals.
- Risk: tokio upgrade may change wake ordering causing subtle races. Mitigation: run extended CI with stress harness and run chaos tests in staging cluster.

Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/slot-allocator-2025
- Design sketch (Figma for sequence diagram): https://www.figma.com/file/slot-allocator-sketch
- Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1834 (allocator core), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1841 (kv-epoch-gc)
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/slot-allocator/canary

Notes:
- This ticket intentionally avoids touching the batching kernel selection; that will be follow-on once allocator and eviction work stabilizes.
